summary:
Round 3, delta only. FIRST, THE CLAIM THAT checkAckOrder's LOGIC IS UNCHANGED: VERIFIED, not taken on trust. review.sh's delta is a real git diff of the round-2 tree against the staged tree, and Invariants.java carries exactly one hunk (@@ -123,6 +123,20 @@), 14 added javadoc lines between two

paragraphs, no deletions and no line inside checkAckOrder touched; AckOrderTest.java carries one hunk (@@ -219,4 +219,93 @@), 89 added lines, no deletions, so no existing assertion was weakened alongside anything. No behaviour moved. FOUR MUTATIONS MEASURED IN THE REVIEWER TREE, baseline 14/14 green: (1) `while (seen.contains(w))` -> `if` fails exactly legalPipeliningAtDepthTHREEIsPERMITTED -- R2's surviving mutation is dead; (2) keying the watermark on 0L instead of e.epoch() (all three sites) fails aSUCCESSORChainAckingOutOfOrderIsCaught AND TWOChainsAtDIFFERENTFloorsAreJudgedSeparately -- my R2a is closed, and the new test does reach the ordering comparison rather than stopping at the own-write arm (epoch 2 confirms 0 and 2, so seen.contains(2) is true and w==1 < 2 fires the second arm); (3) flattening base to a global min fails TWOChainsAtDIFFERENTFloorsAreJudgedSeparately; (4) `+ w` -> `+ base.get(e.epoch())` fails theMessageNamesTheLOWESTUnconfirmedWriteNotTheFloor. Each new test kills a mutation no other test in the file kills. R2b: the floor stays and its cost is now in the javadoc. I CHECKED THE MITIGATION CLAIM RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT: readChain LISTs the log prefix, so a hole is visible rather than a stopping point, and checkChain's gap arm fires on it -- InvariantsTest.aHOLEInTheChainIsReported already pins the exact fixture the javadoc describes (CONTINUE at slot 0, slot 1 never claimed, delta at 2 -> a `chain` violation). The claim is true and backed by a passing test, so the M4.13 note's 'run BOTH checkers' requirement is not a promise about code that does not exist. Cost lens: checkAckOrder issues no get/put/list/stat and touches no store; the delta adds no object-store request of any kind, and nothing in it scales with records, shards, partitions or indices. Scope: no production file staged, no code outside M4.11's surface, and the M4.13 note follows the file's own convention of prose under the heading above the row. I agree with deferring the test reviewer's remaining minor (the own-write arm's message content): the violation is still counted and the seed still fails, only the named slot is wrong, and at round 4 of a 2-round cap the cost of a fifth round exceeds the harm. It belongs in the commit body and closed by an assertion when M4.13 first consumes the string.
